_about: Resolution of the 142 form-vs-declaration conflicts in integration_advice.json, grouped by owning declaration (principal scene / kin / override), decided per-family per Palle's four rules. Only commons/data/principal_artifacts.json was edited.

resolved.rationale: table_display_2m is for FLAT 2D content (rule 3) but neither tenant is flat 2D. composition_artifact is a 2.0x2.0x4.0 primitive-stack tower that brings its own base -> self (rule 1). The 16 buren_col_* are 6m striped Buren courtyard columns you walk among -> room-scale environment -> field (rule 2), pinned via overrides so they win over the now-self principal.

pattern_tunnel_machine (3x3x10 subway-tiled walkthrough) and random_walker_machine (20.7x2.1x20.4) are room-scale spaces you move through -> field (rule 2). The kin note already flags 'self' as a heterogeneous REVIEW placeholder; the other operable machines stay self.

Flat 2D papers (rule 3) — table_display_1m is the family's named tenant ('papers, compositions, readouts'). Form 'self(+pedestal)' is the tall-panel heuristic: a 1.3m 2D paper is tall but does not bring a 3D stand (the table display IS its stand); the bare 'living_paper' measured 0.2m empty (mid-config).

A 2D grid world (CA/arrays/pixels) is a vertical plane -> frame (rule 3, matches principal bed note). The 1x1x1 oracle read (form: self) is the plane synced to a cube cell, not a self-standing volume. The other 11 grid2d_* instances already agree; untouched.

A 2.6x2.4x2.6 MultiMesh 3D graph is a true volume with comparable dims and no base of its own; it needs housing. gridglass is the declared home for discrete/grid worlds. Form 'self' is the tall-rule firing before the volume-rule; a floating graph does not bring its own pedestal.

0.9x0.9x0.9 sculptural specimens (kind:specimen) presented on a plinth, held to the eye. Form 'self(+pedestal)' trips only because h=0.9 is exactly the self threshold; a specimen does not bring its own base, the plinth elevates it. plinth ~ pedestal, both correct presentation.

Mineral-cluster specimens ~0.7-0.9m on a plinth. Form 'cube' is the volume-heuristic (comparable dims) which cannot distinguish specimen-on-plinth from a housed volume; the specimen presentation is intentional, consistent with mesh_grammar.

Art reliefs (kind:relief) are vertical, shallow-depth (0.5m) content mounted against a panel -> table_display is a 2D-content stand, rule-3 compliant (not a 3D housing). Form 'self' misreads the 1.3m height as own-stand; a displayed relief does not stand itself.

Tiny HUD text readouts (make_text_block descendants) are 2D content -> table_display_1m, the family's named tenant. Form 'plinth|podium'/'cube' is the sub-0.2m HUD measurement; these are migration candidates to TextScreen anyway.

NOC oscillation waves; the kin's own prefer_registry note says measured AABBs catch the wave mid-frame. The wave IS the environment -> field is intentional. Form 'self(+pedestal)' is the mid-frame snapshot, not a self-standing object.
An operated workbench (bench + grabbable cube + live matrix) is self-grounded by the workbench convention. Form 'cube' would seal an interactive tool in a vitrine; self is correct.
Horizontal assembly work-surfaces (2.1x0.3x1.6, h=0.3) you operate on. Form 'frame|table_display (stand it up)' misreads a floor/bench surface as wall art; an operated puzzle is self, not hung.
Station/equipment assembly puzzles are horizontal operated surfaces (1.0x0.3x0.8, h=0.3). Same flat-slab misfire as the assembly_line group; self (operated, own footprint) is correct.
Furniture-assembly puzzles (~1.1x0.9x0.6) you build by hand. Form 'cube' would seal them in a case and block assembly; self is correct for an operated puzzle.
Interactive tile puzzles (0.8x0.8x0.8) operated directly. Form 'cube' is the volume-heuristic; a sealed vitrine would prevent play. self (own footprint, operated) is correct.

A recursive fractal tree; registry footprint is 1x3x3 (a 3m tree). The oracle's 0.1x0.1x0.0 (form: plinth|podium) is a pre-growth/empty measurement. openframe (edges-only, 'things that should breathe/grow') is the purpose-built home for growth structures.

An instrument (kind:instrument, integration:self) that is self-grounded like bar_array and step_sequencer. Form 'cube' (0.7x0.2x1.0) would house a read/operated instrument; self is consistent with the instrument convention.

Ambient particle fields (kind:field). A 2.0x1.5x2.0 cloud is not a pedestal object; the doctrine keeps field/apparition unhoused on purpose (housing/pedestal would kill the field). Form 'self(+pedestal)' misreads the cloud extent as own-stand.

resolved.why_ambiguous: A profile is a 1D curve renderer (2.0x1.5x0.3 vertical plane) — flat-ish 2D content, which rule 3 says gets frame/table_display and NEVER a 3D housing. BUT the shadowbox cube-family was purpose-built 'for curves, profiles, single luminous figures' (one open face, dark backlit interior, 0.3m depth suits a backlit curve, not a flat frame). Genuine design-intent-vs-rule-3 tension; whether a shallow backlit shadowbox counts as a forbidden '3D housing' for 2D content is Palle's call. Left untouched.
resolved.rationale: PALLE RULED: shadowbox stays (design intent wins)

verdicts.why_ambiguous: 0.5x0.9x0.3 — not flat, not room-scale. The 0.9m height for a 0.5m board may already include an own base/funnel (rule 1 -> self) or not (pedestal elevates it). Dropping balls is physics, which could suit the tank cube-family. Evidence is inconclusive; taste call, left as declared (pedestal).
